note: Full-window (347-origin) controlled comparison of frozen GAP19 vs research-only V2. Supersedes nothing; the implementation checkpoint remains the authoritative record of the implementation itself and is unchanged (hashes re-verified below).

preserved_checkpoint_files.description: Hashes re-verified identical to MILP_V2_RESEARCH_IMPLEMENTATION_CHECKPOINT_MANIFEST.json. Frozen checkpoint preserved, not modified, by this experiment.

experiment_design.origin_source: stage8_1_full_37_feature_matrix_2024_CORRECTED.csv forecast_start column (the real '347 clean origins across 2024' used elsewhere in this repository)
experiment_design.forecast_engine: LocalBaselineForecastEngine, identical for both optimizer arms at every origin (not an ablation of forecast engines)
experiment_design.station_state: identical warmed-up state per origin for both arms: 80% SOC / 160000 Wh, diesel running 2h, 500 L fuel remaining
experiment_design.terminal_target_wh_formula: compute_terminal_target_wh, imported unmodified from POLARIS_EMS_GAP19_STAGE81_VS_BASELINE_RESEARCH_SIMULATION/run_research_simulation.py (frozen R1/R2 formula)
experiment_design.critical_demand_formula: min(11600.0, demand[t]), the same production formula worker.py uses

1_essential_tier_formulation_effects: essential service fraction ranges 32.2%-100% (mean 50.4%, median 48.5%) across 245 NORMAL origins; no origin has essential_demand_sum == 0
curtailment lower in V2 than GAP19 at all 245/245 origins (mean 130273.4 -> 85954.7 Wh, ~34% reduction)
battery charge AND discharge totals differ at all 245/245 origins, consistently with GAP19 higher -- directional consistency across independent origins indicates causal effect, not noise
GAP19.unmet_load - V2.unmet_load == V2.load_served_essential exactly at every origin, max deviation 7.3e-12 Wh (float noise) -- Rev.3 double-counting fix confirmed on full real window
J4 higher in V2 at every origin (adds unmet_essential term); not interpreted as a performance regression per task instruction
2_solver_tie_breaking_effects: NONE detected on real-data window -- contrasts with the synthetic flat-profile smoke-test finding (checkpoint Scenarios 3 and 5)

diesel dispatch exactly identical between GAP19 and V2 at all 245/245 origins: on-hours count (426=426), startup-event count (220=220), and aggregate sum (0 origins differ by >1e-6 W), checked per-origin not just in aggregate

dispatch_schedule_byte_identical=False at all 245 origins, but fully attributable to the Essential-tier battery effect (finding 1), not tie-breaking, since diesel (the tie-sensitive component in the synthetic tests) is perfectly identical here
conclusion: the degenerate-schedule finding from the implementation checkpoint is specific to artificially flat/constant-profile inputs; real non-flat data shows no evidence of it
3_unchanged_gap19_behavior: J1 (critical deficit) = 0.0 at all 245 origins, both optimizers -- critical load always fully served
J2, J3 bit-identical between GAP19 and V2 at all 245/245 origins (j1_j2_j3_identical=True, 245/245)
diesel dispatch identical at every origin (see finding 2)
demand accounting: 0.0 Wh max error at every origin, both optimizers (served[+served_essential]+unmet==demand, per-hour, all 245 origins)
energy-balance error: 0.0 at every origin, both optimizers
essential balance: 0.0 Wh max error at every origin (served_essential+unmet_essential==essential_demand)

SOC ceiling (95%) reached identically at all 245 origins; SOC floor differs at 19/245 origins as a downstream consequence of finding 1, not a new bound violation; SOC stayed within [20%,95%] at every origin both arms
solver status OPTIMAL at all 245 compared origins; zero infeasibilities in the full window
4_unexpected_v2_behavior: NONE -- zero automated flags raised across all 347 origins (0 infeasibility, 0 objective-stage divergence, 0 demand-accounting error, 0 energy-balance error, 0 diesel-aggregate divergence)

action_taken_on_failure: NONE_REQUIRED -- no invariant failed; V2 was not modified
